title: Wave 8: the desktop app, integrated and fixed
summary: The ARGOS desktop app after the wave 8 fixer, on a DEV build ("ARGOS Dev", org.argos.argos.dev) of the Tauri shell with the one-dir sidecar frozen from the final tree (no PyQt6, no pyqtgraph), running the real web UI in WKWebView. Changed from the integration set: a borderless window with rounded corners and the system shadow (no grey macOS outline: Night Red holds), the title bar with the section only and filled discs at macOS's pitch, the Quit confirmation with text buttons (no hold), one notice for a shutdown asked elsewhere, stage times in tenths, log boxes opened at their last line with columns kept, the start-up failure's Quit ARGOS, the toast's file name on its own line, Cmd+1-Cmd+5 and full screen in the palette, and Night Red captures of every W8 surface in WebKit. Window captures (screencapture -l) at device scale 2, converted from Display P3 to sRGB so the Night Red and brass audits read true colours (Night Red: 6 of 6 pass, rule A 0 px, rule B 0 px; brass 0-16 906 px per shot). Test runs used temporary HOME, TMPDIR, configuration and log folders and the built-in simulator; the Review session is an APFS clone of a recorded XX Cyg session; windows were sized through the window-state plugin's file.

shots.caption: Start-up in the UI's theme: the window shows the UI about 0.5 s after launch, before the server is ready; 'Starting the ARGOS server...' runs, 'Connecting' waits (a server slowed by 4 s on purpose for this capture). Normally the server is spawned first thing (before the window), its ready line comes 1.14-1.26 s after launch and the UI, which adopts it in place without reloading, is connected at about 1.5 s.

Start-up failure in the UI (a server given --sim-replay on a missing folder on purpose): the cause and exit status, the server's last lines with their columns kept (argparse usage) and opened at the end, the log folder breaking only after a slash, then Copy details, Open log folder | Quit ARGOS, Retry (focused). Cmd+Q here quit at once (no server to stop). The default window, fitted to this display's work area.

Connection in the desktop window (fixer build): a borderless window with rounded corners (corner pixels transparent; no grey outline from macOS), the title bar naming only the section, muted, and three filled discs at macOS's 20 px pitch where the traffic lights sit.
Observe, Observatory theme, with the token-drawn title bar.
Observe, Charcoal theme: the title bar follows the theme tokens.

Review R1, opened by the frozen sidecar (argos/core/session/review.py ships in it; the release workflow now proves it with `argos-server --self-check`).
Export CSV with 'Download': the server writes the file and the UI hands it to the webview as a download.

The download saved in Downloads by the shell: the toast's title row carries Reveal in Finder and Dismiss, the file name sits on its own full-width line, never broken at a hyphen (shortened in the middle when too long).
Settings > About in the desktop app: the three link buttons alike, as text (no icon set has a 'source code' symbol), Reveal in Finder after each folder (A12).

Quit during a run (AppleScript 'quit app', which the shell turns into a quit request): A7 refused (409 busy) and the confirmation says what runs in the server's words; text buttons (BRAND 7, 01 2.4.3): Cancel has the focus, Quit ARGOS is the destructive one. Cancel left the run going (3 keep-awake assertions held); Cmd+Q then Quit ARGOS forced it: 202, the server's five stages, exit status 0, window gone 0.7 s later, nothing left.

A shutdown asked by another client during a run: one notice for the event ('The ARGOS server was shut down', no error mark, no log). The stages carry their real times ('< 0.1 s' under a tenth, tenths under 10 s); when the shell then reports the exit (status 0) the panel stays. Restart server brought the UI back on a new server.

Crash notice after a kill -9 of the server during a run: 'stopped unexpectedly (signal 9)', the server's last lines opened at the end with their columns, the log folder; Restart server (focused) had the UI back on a new server; nothing left of the old one (no keep-awake assertion).
